legacy_root.answer: quality.yml has 85 steps that are independent yet sequenced behind a fail-fast predecessor (82 of them checks) across 8 jobs / 108 steps. no-runtime-junk.yml has 3 such steps (the later independent Python gates after checkout+setup-python). Jobs in quality.yml have no `needs:` edges so they already run in parallel; the hiding is intra-job. The densest stack is test-python (69 steps): fail-fast reports 1 defect, the aggregator reports 65 in one run. Counts are from live .github/workflows/*.yml (live-yaml).

detector_control.known_broken_fixture: fail_fast mode on three independent seeded defects
detector_control.procedure: same StepSpec list; fail_fast reports 1 defect and skips the rest; aggregate reports all 3 independent defects and skips only the json-consuming dependent step

legacy_root.evidence_requirement: a step-dependency classification per workflow (independent vs genuinely dependent) with the justification per step, plus a seeded run carrying THREE independent defects that must be reported in ONE run rather than three
legacy_root.notes: G-1 for TST-0016: live named probes exit 0, receipt state=SUCCESS, per-unit manifest row. Did not run global unit_manifest.py --write. cloud ok=true is not delivery. No ADV rebuild. Classification prefers live .github/workflows YAML when PyYAML can parse it, else AUD-0041 captured inventory.

provenance.ci_hygiene_note: rules/common/ci-hygiene.md is present at repo root and was recorded as an input; classification itself walks the workflow YAML, not the rule text

legacy_root.question: A CI job stops at its FIRST failing step, so one red job reports one defect while hiding every later one. Measured on this estate: a single red e2e job was actually FOUR stacked independent failures, discovered only by fixing them one at a time across four round trips. Target: independent checks must run to completion and aggregate their results, so one run reveals the full defect set; only genuinely dependent steps may short-circuit. Question: how many steps in each workflow are independent yet sequenced behind a fail-fast predecessor?
legacy_root.schema_note: catalog names test-receipt.schema.json; that shim exists and $ref's the generated test-receipt profile. G-1 delivery is file+probes+manifest, not a full profile-schema round-trip.

legacy_root.title: Fail-fast gate ordering hides N-1 defects behind the first red step

residual_unknowns.claim: Independent cross-vendor reviewer of this leftover envelope has not been dispatched.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Dispatch a fresh-context reviewer over the catalog output_path after schema-valid write.

answer: quality.yml has 85 steps that are independent yet sequenced behind a fail-fast predecessor (82 of them checks) across 8 jobs / 108 steps. no-runtime-junk.yml has 3 such steps (the later independent Python gates after checkout+setup-python). Jobs in quality.yml have no `needs:` edges so they already run in parallel; the hiding is intra-job. The densest stack is test-python (69 steps): fail-fast reports 1 defect, the aggregator reports 65 in one run. Counts are from live .github/workflows/*.yml (live-yaml).

detector_control.known_broken_fixture: fail_fast mode on three independent seeded defects
detector_control.procedure: same StepSpec list; fail_fast reports 1 defect and skips the rest; aggregate reports all 3 independent defects and skips only the json-consuming dependent step

evidence_requirement: a step-dependency classification per workflow (independent vs genuinely dependent) with the justification per step, plus a seeded run carrying THREE independent defects that must be reported in ONE run rather than three
notes: G-1 for TST-0016: live named probes exit 0, receipt state=SUCCESS, per-unit manifest row. Did not run global unit_manifest.py --write. cloud ok=true is not delivery. No ADV rebuild. Classification prefers live .github/workflows YAML when PyYAML can parse it, else AUD-0041 captured inventory.

provenance.ci_hygiene_note: rules/common/ci-hygiene.md is present at repo root and was recorded as an input; classification itself walks the workflow YAML, not the rule text

question: A CI job stops at its FIRST failing step, so one red job reports one defect while hiding every later one. Measured on this estate: a single red e2e job was actually FOUR stacked independent failures, discovered only by fixing them one at a time across four round trips. Target: independent checks must run to completion and aggregate their results, so one run reveals the full defect set; only genuinely dependent steps may short-circuit. Question: how many steps in each workflow are independent yet sequenced behind a fail-fast predecessor?
schema_note: catalog names test-receipt.schema.json; that shim exists and $ref's the generated test-receipt profile. G-1 delivery is file+probes+manifest, not a full profile-schema round-trip.
